Nagpulong ang Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) at Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) ngayong araw, Setyembre 4, para pag-usapan ang pagkakaroon ng potensyal na proyekto upang mabigyan ng prayoridad ang mga hamon sa pagkontol ng baha.

Sa pagpupulong na pinangunahan ni MMDA Chairman Atty. Don Artes, tinalakay ang posibleng pag-adopt ng "Sponge City" principles sa flood management framework sa Metro Manila.

Nakasaad sa inilatag na konsepto na kinakailangang magdisenyo ng mga lungsod na maaaring sumipsip, mag-imbak, at gumamit muli ng tubig-ulan — tulad ng isang sponge o espongha.

Ang AIIB ay katuwang ng MMDA sa implementasyon ng Metro Manila Flood Management Project Phase 1 na naglalayong mabawasan ang pagbaha sa Kalakhang Maynila sa pamamagitan ng pagpapatupad ng iba't ibang programa ukol sa solid waste management sa mga komunidad. #mmda #mmdaatyourservice

data.english_translation: Today’s Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) and Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIB) meet today, September 4, to discuss the presence of a central project to give priority to the challenges of flooding. At meetings led by MMDA Chadiirman Atty. Dores discussed the possible heading of "Spon City" flood management in the Metro.

PROTESTERS TARGET DISCAYA-OWNED CONSTRUCTION FIRM

Various environmental and progressive groups, along with flood victims, staged a protest on Thursday and vandalized the gates of St. Gerrard Construction, a company owned by the Discayas and linked to alleged anomalous flood control projects with the Department of Public Works and Highways in Pasig City on Thursday.

Protesters splashed mud and spray-painted messages on the gates during the rally.

📸 The STAR/Miguel de Guzman

In a Facebook post, Pasig City Mayor Vico Sotto encouraged everyone not to resort to violence, after a group of protesters stormed the St. Gerrard building owned by the Discayas.

The protesters threw mud, wrote on walls, and shook the gate of a property amid the probe into anomalous flood control projects. They were composed of flood victims and militant groups.

According to the Discayas’ lawyer, Atty. Cornelio Samaniego III, their camp will file a criminal complaint against the organizer of the protest.
